Pere Ubu is one one of my favorite bands. They're an avant-garde art punk band that had a major influence on the post-punk scene in the late seventies. They're still making critically acclaimed albums and have a faithful cult following, but they've never turned a profit. David Thomas, the band's leader, had this to say about the band:

Pere Ubu is not now nor has it ever been a viable commercial venture. We won't sleep on floors, we won't tour endlessly and we're embarrassed by self-promotion. Add to that a laissez-faire attitude to the mechanics of career advancement and a demanding artistic agenda and you've got a recipe for real failure. That has been our one significant success to this date: we are the longest-lasting, most disastrous commercial outfit to ever appear in rock 'n' roll. No one can come close to matching our loss to longevity ratio.

They had the skills to make it big, but I'm happy that they had integrity and didn't compromise their artistic vision.

Although most musical artists want to be able to make a living with their music, not all of them are interested in being "huge", or even being in the center spotlight. And arguably these are the ones who do it because they love it, for 30 years.

Of course one of the problems of being even a moderately successful musician is that not everyone has good money management skills, and if you have a smash hit and have a windfall of cash you become a target for people who know how to take advantage of that.

I'm currently running a 0.09 ohm coil, 360 degrees F @ 30W. I'm loving it but I was wondering if anybody has a better coil build. I'm currently using a 10 wrap n200 standard coil. It seems like a sleeper coil would work better in a temp controlled mod, but I haven't tried it yet. Any thoughts?

You can probably stand to increase the temperature to closer to 400F. What's your atomizer? I found in my Rose V2-S that having as fat an inner diameter as possible and doubled over legs helped out a ton with resistance stability, so I'm not tripping into temp limit all the time.
I have the twisted messes one. And I have turned it up to 400 since I posted this. What do you mean doubled over legs?
Leave your leads extra long, bend them over and crimp them in half, then feed them through the post holes. It won't impact resistance, but it can give you a more stable connection.
I try to go as big as possible with nickel. I do 15 wraps at 3mm of 28g. In a lemo 2, I can really put out some vapor if I want to.

The Kingdom of Rhodesia is a sovereign state in southern Africa, which consists of seven provinces and thirty counties. The Kingdom was founded in 1649 through the popular election of King Francis I of the House of Rhodes, the bastard child of Elizabeth I of England and Sir Francis Drake. The country became a parliamentary state in 1705 after a year long civil war, and was invaded by the British in 1799, but peace was reached in 1814 when Rhodesia agreed to let go of many border claims throughout Southern Africa. After the Berlin Conference in 1885, another civil war broke out when Rhodesia submitted to foreign pressure and dropped more claimed territory, which ultimately resulted in the foundation of the modern unitary government through its expansion in services. After remaining neutral in the First World War, Rhodesia suffered severe economic disorder with the Great Depression, which would see the election of the Social Democrats in 1935 who would retain power to this day. Neutral during the Cold War, Rhodesia soon took on the role of overseeing decolonisation and the pacification of rebel movements throughout Africa. By 2003, the government expanded its peacekeeping role to counter-terrorism efforts worldwide, which, to this day, Rhodesia retains an active role in.

In the Kingdom of Ice- Hampton Sides

 

  An adventure story about polar exploration in the late 1800's. It's extremely well written and had me turning pages for hours on end. The personalities of the crewmates plus their lust for adventure just created a wonderful story that made me more interested in the history of the area.

Lusting for books you've never had, huh? Why not try a classic, a primary source?. Perhaps you're dubious. Perhaps you're skeptical. Let's just cut to the lust -- pics of my junk.
